title: Deep Learning and Computational Physics (lecture notes)
byline: Deep Ray, Orazio Pinti and Assad A. Oberai · USC course notes, 2023
note: Course notes rather than a polished book; sections often end with questions for the reader. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: These notes teach deep learning to people who already know numerical methods for physics, and keep drawing the parallel between the two. Networks are introduced as function approximators with universal approximation results; ResNets are read as time-stepping schemes, which leads to neural ODEs; convolutions are compared with finite-difference stencils. The physics-specific core is solving PDEs with networks: physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that put the PDE residual in the loss, then operator networks (DeepONet and the Fourier Neural Operator) that learn the whole map from inputs to solutions. The last chapter adds probability and generative models (GANs) for problems with uncertain or multiple answers.
